summary: OwnDashboard renders DNESKAi decks through the vendored @boardlessai/carousel-studio (Quorum 852c2e9, tree af3c47dd, byte-identical to a fresh rebuild of that commit and unchanged on Quorum main 76314a3). The path is small and strict: dneskai-slides/1 (1-10 slides, a carousel needs 2+, a single post is one `single` slide, images by sha256 with focal/zoom 1-4/fit), a per-slide render key (dneskai-render-key/2: studio pin, policy dneskai-render/2, sharp/libvips + JPEG settings, trimmed words, variant, image hashes and crops, position), one immutable JPEG per key in the private marketing-assets bucket, and a gate that refuses the whole deck on clipped text, a glyph the field's face lacks, unplaced text or any studio blocking problem. Measured on this machine (Apple M2, 8 GB): a 7-slide deck renders and encodes in 0.63-0.95 s cold and 0.49-0.65 s warm (cover 161-236 ms warm, statement 31-52 ms), 820 KB of JPEG; five kits would be 35 slides, about 2.4-2.7 s of CPU and 4.1 MB. The 21 render/vendor/slides tests pass in 11.6 s. Weak points are around it, not in it: there is no render-only preview (every look at a crop is a saved revision), every design change crosses two repositories in about nine manual steps, the deck/key/tables have no kit dimension, storage round trips (4 per new slide, 3 per cache hit, sequential) not CPU would dominate a five-kit pre-render, the vendor script's --write breaks on macOS after it has already replaced the tree, only 4:5 is composed and nothing previews the 3:4 profile grid, and nothing purges rendered slides.

findings.title: A five-kit pre-render is cheap in CPU but storage round trips would dominate: 4 sequential calls per new slide
findings.claim: Measured CPU for 35 slides is about 2.4-2.7 s, but each newly rendered slide is stored sequentially with upload, info, download (sha256 re-check) and sign, and every cache hit does info, download and sign. Five kits of a 7-slide deck mean 140 sequential storage calls on first render and 105 on an unchanged re-render, inside a job capped at 45 s together with two model attempts.

evidence.excerpt: const uploaded = await files.upload(key, bytes, { upsert: false, contentType: "image/jpeg", cacheControl: "3600", metadata });

findings.recommendation: Render alternative kits outside the generation job (lazy on first view through the preview route of REN-01, or one kit per later tick), store with bounded parallelism (e.g. 4), and skip the re-download on find when the object's recorded sha256 and size match (verify bytes at publish time, which the publisher already does). Measure one real storage round trip on Preview before deciding.
findings.impactStatement: At an estimated 50-150 ms per Supabase storage call (not measured; production has 0 rendered objects), a five-kit first render adds about 7-21 s of I/O to the job and a re-render 5-16 s; that eats the job budget and risks worker-timeout on the second model attempt. Pre-rendering all kits in the generation job is therefore the wrong place; on demand or in a later tick fits.

truth.evidence: Stores are sequential (dneskai-render.ts:393-405) and each put does upload, info, download, sign (worker-runtime.ts:177-182). But cache lookups run in parallel (dneskai-render.ts:353 Promise.all over all keys), so an unchanged re-render is 35 parallel finds of 3 sequential calls each, not 105 sequential calls. Per-call latency is an estimate; production has 0 objects in marketing-assets.

findings.title: vendor-carousel-studio.sh --write breaks on macOS after it has already replaced the vendored tree
findings.claim: The script deletes and replaces vendor/carousel-studio first and only then rewrites UPSTREAM.md with GNU `sed -i "s/…/"`. BSD sed on the owner's Mac reads the expression as the backup suffix and fails, so `set -e` stops with a new tree and a stale pin; the vendor test then fails on the tree hash.
findings.recommendation: Use a portable rewrite (node -e or perl -pi, or `sed -i.bak` then remove the backup) and update UPSTREAM.md in the scratch output before swapping the tree in.
findings.impactStatement: A re-vendor on the owner's machine leaves the repository half-updated; recoverable with git checkout, but it costs a confused hour the first time and makes the cross-repo loop (REN-02) more fragile.

truth.evidence: vendor-carousel-studio.sh:91-92 replace the tree before :95 runs `sed -i "s/..." "$upstream_doc"`; with set -euo pipefail (:19) a sed failure exits. Reproduced the same sed -i form with macOS /usr/bin/sed: exit 1, 'undefined label'. No CI job runs --write (grep vendor-carousel .github finds none), so the Mac is where it runs.

impact.reason: A tiny fix that saves a broken re-vendor during the coming kit work; low impact on its own.
